fairness.title: Fairness — How STACK Verifies Results | STACK
fairness.description: How results are decided on STACK, which games are server-verified, and what is still in progress.
fairness.intro: The client is never trusted. Here is exactly what is verified today.

p: Slither, Agar, Hole, Paper, Chicken and Storm Royale, Road Cross and Flappy Cash all run on the server. Your browser only sends inputs (steering, shooting, hopping, flapping) and draws the state the server sends back. The server simulates the match, picks the seeds, checks every input and pays the winner, so a modified browser cannot change an outcome.
A bet is priced from the server's own cached odds line at the moment you place it. Settlement is automatic, and a bet can only be paid out once.
Every balance change runs in a database transaction with a row lock and is written to an audit ledger.

A server cannot tell a person from a bot that plays through the normal controls, and it does not hide other players positions from your client, so aim assistants and map hacks are possible in shooters. The classic casino games (Dice and the rest) are not server-verified yet and will be before any real-money launch.

posts.title: What Is House Edge? A Plain-English Guide
posts.description: House edge explained with real examples: how casinos make money, why long-run results follow the math, and how to compare games.
body: House edge is the average percentage of each bet the casino keeps over the long run. If a game has a 1% edge, then on average you lose 1 credit for every 100 wagered.
It is an average, not a promise. Short sessions swing wildly; over thousands of bets results converge toward the math. That is why a game can pay out today and still be a losing game overall.

To compare games, look at the edge, not the theme. Single-zero (European) roulette has a 2.7% edge. Blackjack with good basic strategy can be under 1%. Slots typically sit between 2% and 8% depending on the game.
Bet size does not change the edge, but it changes how much you lose per hour. A 1% edge on 10 credits a spin costs less per hour than the same edge on 100 credits.
The practical takeaway: pick lower-edge games if you want your money to last, set a budget first, and treat any win as luck rather than skill.

posts.title: Provably Fair Explained: Can You Verify a Casino Result?
posts.description: How seeds, hashes and server-side replays let you check that a casino game was not rigged, and where the limits of that promise are.
body: Provably fair means the outcome of a round can be checked after the fact instead of taken on trust.
The classic approach commits to a secret server seed by publishing its hash before you play. After the round the seed is revealed and you can confirm it matches the hash and reproduces the outcome.

A second approach, used for Slither Royale on STACK, is server-side replay: the server picks the seed, records your inputs, and re-simulates the round with the same engine. The payout depends only on that replay, so a tampered browser cannot change the result.
Neither method proves the odds are generous. It proves the result was not changed after you bet. You still need to read the game's house edge.
Verify what you can, and remember that fair does not mean profitable.

posts.title: Bankroll Management Basics: Setting Limits That Work
posts.description: Simple, practical rules for setting a gambling budget, session limits and stop points so gambling stays entertainment.
body: A bankroll is money set aside only for entertainment. If losing it would affect rent, food or bills, it is not a bankroll.
Set three limits before playing: a total budget, a maximum stake per bet (many people use 1–2% of the budget), and a time limit. Write them down.
Decide your stop points in advance. Walk away when you hit the loss limit, and consider stopping after a large win too, because the next bets are still negative on average.
Never chase losses. Raising stakes to win money back is the fastest way to turn a small loss into a large one.
If you notice you cannot stick to your limits, take a break and see the Responsible Gambling page for free support.
